newsitem.title: USA: Mexico's recovery to continue in 1997, Rubin says.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's recovery to continue in 1997, Rubin says.

text.p: Mexico's economic recovery continued in the third quarter, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin told Congress in a report on Friday that said solid growth was foreseen for 1997.

"Both the Mexican government and private analysts expect solid growth to continue next year," Rubin said in a foreword to the monthly report on Mexico's progress in working out of a financial crisis with U.S. financial aid.
Rubin said Mexico's financial markets strengthened in November as Mexican authorities maintained "solid" monetary and fiscal policies aimed at curbing inflation.
Mexico's hard-pressed banking sector still was restructuring in November, with the level of bad loans down slightly but still high, Rubin said.
An estimated 12 percent of all loans made by private banks were ranked as non-performing in September -- the latest month for which statistics were available -- compared with 12.7 percent in August.

The United States signed an agreement with Mexico in February 1995 to provide up to $20 billion of aid but Mexico did not draw it all. Rubin said Mexico still owes $3.5 billion but was "well ahead of schedule" in paying it back.
Rubin said Mexico's real gross domestic product grew by 7.4 percent in the third quarter compared with a year earlier when the country was enduring a deep recession.
Private analysts have forecast real GDP growth for Mexico of 4.2 percent in 1997, Rubin noted.
